subject: Notice: us-west-2 failover dry-run and kernel alignment window (Aug 25)
raw:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: us-west-2 failover dry-run and kernel alignment window (Aug 25)

Hi Samantha / Acme ops team,

We wanted to let you know about a planned failover dry-run and kernel/driver alignment window we have scheduled for the us-west-2 region on Tuesday, August 25. This is a non-emergency, pre-emptive exercise to validate cross-availability failover and ensure driver compatibility across the fleet after our recent kernel microcode updates.

Planned window:
- Start: 2026-08-25 02:00 PDT
- End: 2026-08-25 05:00 PDT
- Expected customer-facing impact: minimal. We will run controlled canaries and surgical instance evacuations. In the unlikely event of higher error rates, we will fail back immediately to prior kernels.

What to expect from Redwood:
- Canary traffic to a small subset of your serving hosts first (no routing changes expected).
- Driver/kernel swap on a rolling subset with KV cache warmup preserved where possible.
- Automatic rollback policy if token error rate or latency exceeds thresholds defined in the attached checklist.

Attachments: dryrun-checklist.pdf, failover-playbook-v2.docx
Runbook link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/failover-playbook

Action requested:
- Please confirm if the window is acceptable for Acme (reply to this thread).
- If you want a 30-minute readiness call, tell us your preferred time on Aug 24.

Thanks — we aim to keep this low-friction and will communicate any change immediately.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: internal: us-west-2 dry-run coordination

Marissa — looping in a couple of operational notes so the customer stays in the loop but we keep internal playbook actionable: 

- Canary plan: 5% of Acme's nodes targeted first across both AZs; monitor p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate. Thresholds and rollback criteria are in failover-playbook-v2.docx.
- KV cache preservation: we will use warm-warm handoffs for nodes that support persistent kvcache; some older hosts will require KV re-warm, which may briefly affect tail latency.
- Rollback: immediate rollback if 5xxs > 0.5% sustained for 2 minutes OR p95 > baseline + 200ms for more than 3 minutes.

Please confirm you will host the readiness call Aug 24 11:00 PDT (Samantha confirmed). I will prepare a short runthrough deck and bring SRE on the line (Marcus).

Ben Carter
Director of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Notice: us-west-2 failover dry-run and kernel alignment window (Aug 25) — confirmation and dial-in

Hi Samantha / Acme ops team,

Thanks for confirming and for the window preference — we've adjusted the canary schedule to avoid the 02:30–03:15 PDT batch peak. Confirm final plan below: 

Final plan summary:
- Dry-run window: 02:00–05:00 PDT, Aug 25.
- Canary activity: 02:00–02:30 (5% of nodes)
- Bulk rolling: 02:40–04:50 (staggered across AZs to prevent simultaneous KV warming)
- Monitoring and rollback gates enforced throughout.

Readiness call: Aug 24, 11:00 PDT — Zoom link: https://zoom.us/j/987654321 (invite will follow).

Attachments included again for convenience: dryrun-checklist.pdf, failover-playbook-v2.docx

We will post a short post-exercise note within 2 hours of completion summarizing observations and any follow-ons. If anything changes before the window, you'll get an immediate update.

Best regards,
